messages:
From: Kenji Saito <kenji@orbithelm.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-07T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Prompt Orchestration Adapter — Orbit Helm x Redwood

Hi Soojin,

Longtime fan of Redwood — congrats on the Dedicated launch. Orbit Helm builds a prompt orchestration layer used by several ISVs; our customers love the way we do dynamic prompt routing, multi-model fan-out and scoring. We think there’s a good fit to build a lightweight adapter that plugs Orbit Helm into Redwood’s runtime and exposes trace events back into our tracing UI and (critically) into LangChain/LlamaIndex SDK integrations.

Proposal in one line: a 3-week pilot to ship an adapter that routes prompts from Orbit Helm to a pinned Redwood model, forwards token-level traces, and supports a LangChain/LlamaIndex middleware hook for attribution. Benefits to Redwood: increased usage across our ISV customers, an easy way to show interop with popular SDKs, and per-request trace visibility.

Ask: can you share your SOC2 summary and a short list of technical acceptance criteria (SSO, certs, staging endpoints)? I attached a short mutual action plan we usually use for pilots.

We’re flexible on kickoff dates — earliest next Monday.

Thanks,
Kenji
Head of Partnerships | Orbit Helm

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-06-07T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prompt Orchestration Adapter — Orbit Helm x Redwood

Kenji — really appreciate the intro and the clear one-line proposal. This is squarely in our ISV partner playbook. Quick responses below and a couple of asks from our side: 

- SOC2 & security: please send your completed security questionnaire (or the filled template) and any pen-test summaries. We’ll need a reviewed copy for our compliance team.
- Pilot scope: 3 weeks works for a technical pilot. For outcomes we want: (1) proof of request routing into Redwood, (2) token-level trace / KV cache visibility surfaced back to Orbit Helm, (3) a small LangChain/LlamaIndex example (not full SDK integration) that demonstrates attribution headers.
- Staging: we can provision a short-lived staging API key and a dedicated staging pool for the pilot if you sign the MAA.

I’m looping in Vanessa (partnerships lead) and Marissa (ISV enablement) to coordinate resources and a kickoff date. Can you confirm your engineering lead and availability next week?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Partner Integrations | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-06-07T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prompt Orchestration Adapter — Orbit Helm x Redwood

Kenji — excited to dig in. A few technical points to speed the pilot: 

1) LangChain/LlamaIndex hooks: our recommendation is to implement a middleware shim that attaches two headers (X-Redwood-Request-Id, X-Redwood-Model-Version) and emits a compact trace event via our ingest endpoint. We can provide a reference Python snippet.

2) Tracing schema: we prefer token-level events in our proto but accept JSON-LD for the pilot. Can you confirm whether Orbit Helm currently emits token deltas? If not, we can accept per-request aggregated timings as a fallback.

3) Authentication/attestation: for staging we support API keys or mTLS; for production we’ll require customer-specific routing rules and a short onboarding questionnaire.

4) Acceptance checklist (proposed):
   - adapter routes >100 QPS in staging without error spikes
   - trace events appear in Orbit Helm UI and in Redwood Console debug traces
   - LangChain example notebook validates attribution headers

We can host a 45-minute technical kickoff Thurs (Jun 10) at 10am PT — does that work? I’ve created a Drive folder for shared artifacts and a short MAA doc (link below).

Marissa Cole
ISV Enablement Lead | Redwood Inference

Kenji
